root_cause: Feature, not a bug: ValidationException subclasses (RequestValidationError, WebSocketRequestValidationError, ResponseValidationError) carried only the error list, and only ResponseValidationError had a __str__ (always plural 'validation errors'). Nothing recorded which endpoint raised the error, so server-side tracebacks could not point at the handler.
best_solution:
In fastapi/exceptions.py add a TypedDict EndpointContext(total=False) with function/path/file/line. Give ValidationException.__init__(errors, *, endpoint_ctx=None), store it plus endpoint_function/path/file/line attributes, and move __str__ up into the base class: '<n> validation error' plus 's' only when n != 1, then one '  {err}' line per error, then a context block. If file, line and function are all known, append '
  File "<file>", line <line>, in <function>' followed by '
    <path>' when a path exists. If only the path is known, append '
  Endpoint: <path>'. Otherwise append nothing. rstrip the result. All three subclasses accept and forward endpoint_ctx as a keyword. In fastapi/routing.py add _extract_endpoint_context(func), cached by id(func), that uses inspect.getsourcefile/getsourcelines/__name__ inside a try/except. In get_request_handler's inner app, and in get_websocket_app, build the ctx from dependant.call and set ctx['path'] = f'{request.method} {root_path.rstrip("/")}{dependant.path}' (or 'WS ...' for websockets). The route template plus root_path is what makes mounted sub-apps show '/sub/items/'. Pass endpoint_ctx= into every RequestValidationError / WebSocketRequestValidationError raise, and thread a new endpoint_ctx kwarg through serialize_response to the ResponseValidationError raise.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_validation_error_context.py (7 tests). It constructs RequestValidationError(errors, endpoint_ctx={'path': 'GET /api/test'}) directly and asserts 'Endpoint: GET /api/test' in str(exc) and 'File "' not in it. It constructs RequestValidationError(errors, endpoint_ctx={}) and asserts '1 validation error:' (singular) with no 'Endpoint' or 'File "'. Through a TestClient with exception handlers registered on app and on a mounted sub_app at /sub, str(exc) must contain the function name and route for: a request path-param error (get_user, '/users/'), a response_model error (get_item, '/items/'), a websocket path-param error (websocket_endpoint, '/ws/'), a sub-app response error (get_sub_item, '/sub/items/') and a sub-app websocket error (subapp_websocket_endpoint, '/sub/ws/'). The kwarg name endpoint_ctx (a dict), the 'Endpoint: ' fallback format and the singular/plural rule never appear as names in the statement.
locating_signals: The statement names the three exception classes (RequestValidationError, ResponseValidationError, WebSocketRequestValidationError), which leads to fastapi/exceptions.py, and the 'Before/After' str() output shows the exact File/line/in format and the 'METHOD /route' line. 'extracted once per endpoint and then cached' points to the request handler factories in routing.py (get_request_handler, get_websocket_app, serialize_response). No function or parameter is named. The key name endpoint_ctx, the TypedDict and the path-only fallback are hidden.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env. v4 got 3/7: it added an endpoint_context: str kwarg (the tests call endpoint_ctx=dict, so TypeError on the 2 direct-construction tests), kept the plural 'validation errors' text, and in get_request_handler passed endpoint=route.endpoint, method=scope['method'] to serialize_response even though neither route nor scope exists in that closure. That raised a NameError instead of ResponseValidationError, so the handler never captured anything on /items/ and /sub/items/. It also left junk test.py/test_context.py files in the repo root. v6 inserted an @lru_cache def into the middle of the 'from fastapi.exceptions import (' statement in routing.py, which is a SyntaxError (unmatched ')'), so collection failed. It also lru_cached on (dependant, request), which is unhashable/per-request, and referenced an undefined endpoint_context in serialize_response. v7 wrote literal backslash-escaped quotes (f\"...\") into exceptions.py (SyntaxError), never touched routing.py, and left a duplicate __str__ in place. v8 produced only a scratch test_exceptions.py with no source change, so all 7 tests failed.
generalizable_lesson: When a feature's tests will construct your new exception or object directly, the keyword name is the API. Pick the name the statement's wording implies, and when the statement gives an exact str() rendering, copy it character for character, including singular/plural ('1 validation error:'). Build a rendering that degrades gracefully when fields are missing. Prefer a dict/TypedDict context over a pre-formatted string so partial data still renders. Only thread values that are actually in scope in the closure you are editing: read the enclosing function signature before referencing route/scope/request. After any edit to an import block or string literals, run python -m py_compile on the file, and delete scratch files before finishing. Two of four runs died on SyntaxErrors that a compile check would have caught in one second.
acceptable_alternatives: Any object type works for endpoint_ctx as long as it accepts a dict with optional function/path/file/line keys. The cache can be keyed on the function object or on id(func), or computed once at route-build time in APIRoute.__init__ and closed over. The path must be the route template (dependant.path or route.path) prefixed with the mount root_path, not the concrete request URL, although tests only check substrings like '/users/' and '/sub/items/', so request.url.path would also pass. ValidationException.__str__ must live on the base class so request and websocket errors render context too.
